countDefinition: New Rust test functions relative to baseline, including adapted behavioral cases and derived edge cases; not an upstream feature parity percentage.
notes: Derived cases extend the cited contract for Rust transport, admission, byte budgets or failure modes; they are not claimed as identical upstream tests.
Rust Origin policy trusts the bound IP and localhost; other loopback addresses need explicit permission.
Upload process tests isolate simultaneously open transfers but fence individual frames: Rust currently admits only one filesystem blocking job at a time.
Physical-send tests exercise Rust queue permits and cancellation, not a direct port of JavaScript send callback mechanics.
Counts are new Rust test functions, not a count of distinct Paseo tests or a feature coverage percentage.
Every primary reference is a literal test title in the pinned upstream checkout and was validated to occur exactly once in its cited file.
Adapted cases implement a supported Rust contract at its own layer; derived cases extend a cited contract with a Rust boundary, fault or documented difference.
No testcase in this manifest calls a real model service, consumes tokens, uses stored provider credentials or validates a live OpenAI account.
Provider capabilities absent from Rust remain absent: nonblocking questions, rich tool projection, plan mode, multimodal prompts and unimplemented provider adapters are not claimed.

Root subsequently confirmed all 146 added cases passed in the complete instrumented suite after the ordering/budget fixes. Two final transport test-precision edits (normal-request write probe and bytewise-producer naming) were made afterwards; their final full validation and coverage are owned by root. This subagent ran no Cargo command for those final edits.
Counts are Rust test functions, not distinct upstream test counts or feature coverage percentages.
Adapted cases use Rust service/connection contracts. Several combine or extend related upstream assertions.
Derived cases identify a related upstream contract but do not claim that Paseo has that exact edge test.
File IDs explicitly supplied by clients retain replacement compatibility; generated IDs have independent lifetimes.
Local Unix automation tests use fixture-owned subprocesses and loopback ports, without external services.
Label review adds bounded-document/admission regressions. Locked before-image plus real failed-commit recovery are covered; the old list-to-lock scheduling race was not deterministically reproduced.

Checkout polling regressions derive contention, cancellation, tracked-drain, and foreground admission isolation checks from the owned diff observation contract; upstream does not assert Rust semaphore scheduling.
Counts are independent Rust test functions, not upstream unique-test counts or feature coverage percentages. Parameter table rows do not increase the Rust count.
All Rust test names and line numbers are validated against current source; upstream titles and line numbers are validated against the pinned local Paseo source.

Adapted cases test the same externally observable behavior through Rust interfaces and may extend boundary assertions. Derived cases only use the named upstream case as a related contract; they do not claim an exact Paseo test port.
Parameterized browser-tool cases preserve the real upstream title template and named table parameter. Browser protocol tests do not imply native agent tool registration or text response rendering.
Rust physical host leases reclaim browser affinity through successful list results; upstream stable-host reconnect semantics are not claimed.
Schedule fault, capacity and independent calendar-oracle cases are explicitly derived extensions. Schedule record identity/recovery cases do not claim upstream workspace archive orchestration.

Voice uses bounded buffered utterances. Dictation finalization retranscribes retained audio rather than implementing Paseo native streaming STT segment stitching, confidence/filler filters or segment-final semantics.

This manifest includes the 100 tests in the frozen Browser/Schedule/Voice batch. Scoped lint passed; all 153 scoped tests passed across the final crate runs. Root owns final workspace coverage measurement.
Rust test-function counts do not represent unique upstream test coverage or interface implementation percentage.
All upstream titles and line numbers verified against pinned Paseo; table rows remain one Rust test.
All CLI calls use fixture-owned executables and temporary local repositories, never real gh authentication or remote operations.

Rust has no Paseo pluggable forge registry, host probes, SSH alias resolution, TTL caches, poll batching, merge facts/policy validation, PR attachment image rewriting or failed-job log fetching. These remain gaps rather than test ports.
Worktree tests use fixture-owned local Git repositories, including a local bare origin, without remote account access.
Recovery cases exercise the existing low-level adapter; service-level recovery and first-agent branch naming parity are not implied.
